question.problem:
Given that 
$A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -1 \\ -6 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]$
has the LU decomposition $A=LU,$ then $L=$
question.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -1 \\ -6 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}.\end{aligned}
$$
